prose: TechCrunch profiles Mach9's pivot: founded in 2021 as Mach9 Robotics to speed up civil-engineering visual inspections with hardware, co-founder Alex Baikovitz realized the bottleneck was not the scanners but the workflows turning laser-scanner and image data into usable surveys. The company dropped 'Robotics' and rebuilt as AI-powered CAD software for civil engineering, racking up nearly 100 private-beta customers across more than 2,500 projects. The $34 million Series A is co-led by First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Prudence and Quiet Capital participating, as several startups race to modernize the planning-to-building pipeline.
highlights: Mach9: $34M Series A co-led by First Round and Bessemer
Pivot: from robotics hardware to AI CAD for civil engineering
Founder's insight: the pain was workflows, not scanning hardware
Prudence and Quiet Capital also in the round
